stem: Users were randomised when they first reached the checkout. To compute conversion per variant, an analyst counts every purchase each test user made in the test month, including purchases made before the user was assigned. What does this do to the comparison?

options.text: It breaks the randomisation, so the two variants end up unequal in size and cannot be compared
It counts purchases the variant cannot have caused, which blurs the effect being measured
It raises only the treatment group's rate, so the measured lift comes out overstated
It is the right method, because the whole test month is the period being measured
